name: gimex::fsh::EncodeColourBlock (fsh_encode_colour_block)
notes: Lane MS. GimexFshEncodeColour_Block: 60,000 seeded 4x4 blocks (and narrower, shorter ones), outputs and every byte written compared, the original and ours each run with 16 KB of cleared stack. The original reads uninitialised stack here (the 3-colour pass classifies chosen[k], the colour the 4-colour pass picked, not the palette colour; the 4-colour pass is skipped for blocks with a pixel below alpha 0x40, so chosen, the weights past the palette's end and the index slots of a block narrower than 4 are garbage); ours zero-initialises, and equals the original with a cleared stack (probe: 6,580 of 15,257 transparent blocks with more than 2 colours changed with the stack filling, none of the opaque or two-colour ones). ORIGINAL-BUG markers on the chosen read and on the 3-colour middle ((a + b) * 0x5555 >> 16, a third of the sum). Mutants (tools/mutate.py, filter gz_gimex_fsh_encode_colour): 15 over the colour group, 13 killed, 2 equivalent (kThirdsRound 0x5555 to 0x5554: 43690x + 21845 is odd, never a multiple of 2^17, so the shift is unchanged; the 2-colour swap with <= to <: two distinct palette entries never pack to the same 16-bit value). matchcheck v8: no match (frame and spill differences). Hooked at its RVA (src/hook/tables/GimexFshEncode.cpp).

name: gimex::fsh::FitAlpha (fsh_fit_alpha)
notes: Lane MS. GimexFshEncodeFit_Alpha: 30,000 seeded value sets (all-equal, 0/1-only, mixed), outputs and the whole global window 0x10e8000..0x10ee000 compared, the stack cleared before each call. The original reads stale stack when a candidate list is empty (all values exactly 1, or exactly 0 or 1): the solver writes nothing for it yet the candidate can win; ours keeps 0 (ORIGINAL-BUG marker; not checked against a decoder that 0 decodes right). Mutants (filter gz_gimex_fsh_encode_fit): tie to >=, the allow-zero test, the table of lists using one, the enabled test, the code for one, the list for neither: 6 killed by Alpha and Blocks. Hooked at its RVA.

name: gimex::fsh::FitColours (fsh_fit_colours)
notes: Lane MS. GimexFshEncodeFit_Colours: 20,000 seeded colour sets (1..16 colours; all close, one, two, few, many distinct colours), outputs and the whole global window compared bit-exact (doubles compared by memcmp), the stack cleared before each call. Control flow transcribed from the disassembly: the persistent found flag, the 17th-try special case, the lastPass fix-up, the out-of-range check and the bounded retry (up to 9). Mutants (filter gz_gimex_fsh_encode_fit): errors tie in the lastPass choice, the lower-bound comparison, the dropped mean, the level count per pass: 4 killed by Colours and Blocks. The pass loops' try cap (old == 0 to old == 1, both the two-pass loop and the bounded retry) is reached by no random case (3,000,000 cases of 8..16 colours: at most 11 of 17 tries), so GimexFshEncodeFit_ColoursSearchCap stands a function that never reports a repeat in for the same-order test 0x89c42d and a rotating ordering for 0x89d691 (CodePatch over the image, so both sides run every search to its cap with different results per try); both cap mutants are killed by it (with the reorder not stood in, the orderings reach a fixed point and the last try repeats the earlier result: the mutants survived). Hooked at its RVA.

name: gimex::fsh::EncodeBlocks (fsh_encode_blocks)
notes: Lane MS. GimexFshEncodeFit_Blocks: 6,000 seeded images (widths and heights 0..13, pitches with padding, the Flat/Gradient/Noise/Edges/FewColours/TwoColours/Translucent looks, kinds 0/0x100/0x200/0x300, modes 0..2, 565 and 4444 forms, both byte orders), half single blocks and half multi-block (kind 0x200 there with alpha 1..254: an empty candidate list reads stale stack, see 0x897b56); returned size, output bytes, source and the whole global window compared, the stack cleared before each call. Modes above 2 and multi-block alpha with empty lists are not tested (stale slots and stack). Mutants (filter gz_gimex_fsh_encode_fit): 11 over the driver, 9 killed by Blocks (alpha swap condition and codes, the fit's level cap, the colour swap bit, mode 2's alpha floor, the code shift, the 4444 shift, the end-point bump), 2 equivalent (the 4-bit alpha rounding 0x80 to 0x7f: 15a mod 255 is a multiple of 15, never 127; the swap test ends[1] <= ends[0]: equal end points were made different just before). A one-byte difference at 0x10ebdc8 (the solver 0x899d55's threshold scratch, outputs identical) in two early runs was not seen in 40+ later runs; likely cause (not proven): the solver builds a double from a stack local it never writes, and in several-block calls the stack differs between the sides. The test leaves exactly 0x10ebdc8..0x10ebe00 out of the global comparison for the several-block cases (nothing else reads it); one-block cases still compare it. The 6-level alpha code swap (swapped = 7 - code, codes 2..5) is unreachable with the real solver: the driver swaps a 6-level pair only when e0 > e1, and over 300,000 random alpha fits the solver always returned e0 <= e1 (6 and 8 levels alike; 8 levels are always swapped, which Blocks covers, the 9 - code mutant dies there). GimexFshEncodeFit_BlocksAlphaSwap puts a stand-in solver returning the 6-level end points reversed over the image's 0x899d55 (both sides call it), 1500 alpha images with codes 0..5: the 7 - code to 8 - code mutant is killed by it only. Hooked at its RVA.
